en.title: Simple comparisons
en.goal: Make basic comparisons between people, objects and situations.

lessons.diferente-melhor: Saying what is different or the best

phrases.t: This one and that one are the same.
Which do you think is the best?

dialogue.title: Comparing languages
lines: Do you think Chinese is hard?
Chinese is even harder than French, but it's really interesting.
Which do you think is the hardest? Chinese or Italian?

bi-comparison.title: 比 (bǐ) — making comparisons
bi-comparison.body: 比 (bǐ) is used to compare two things, working like "more... than" in English. The structure is: A + 比 + B + Adjective.

bi-comparison.title: "Bǐ" or "yíyàng"?
bi-comparison.body: Bǐ compares a difference between two things. Yíyàng (一样) says that two things are the same. Note that "bù yíyàng" (not the same) does not use bǐ — they are two separate structures and don't mix.
examples: this one and that one are the same

haishi.title: 还是 (háishi) — "or" in choice questions
haishi.body: 还是 (háishi) is used to offer two options in a question, like "or" when you expect the person to choose between one thing and the other — unlike 或者, which is used outside of questions.
examples: do you want tea or coffee?
